finding.title: Scope DataExportImportService.importData()'s 16 bare table deletes to the imported profile, not every profile on the device

evidence.quote:
/// Per-profile import: deletes all existing rows and re-inserts from the
  /// export payload. Does not hard-delete accounts not present in the export

finding.why: Every delete in importData() (lines 517-532, one per user-data table) calls Drift's `delete(table).go()` with no `.where()` clause, which executes an unconditional DELETE FROM on that table. On a device with more than one local account or learner profile (the app's own account-switcher/registry and sibling-profile model), importing ONE profile's exported JSON silently erases every OTHER profile's/account's rows in all 16 tables first -- directly contradicting the method's own doc comment. The multi-account round-trip test (epic_26_story_23_data_export_round_trip_test.dart) can't catch this because it manually wipes the ENTIRE database before calling importData(), so a scoped delete and this unscoped one are indistinguishable to that test. DataExportImportService has zero production callers today (grepped repo-wide across lib/), so no user is exposed yet, but it is fully implemented and covered by ~900 lines of tests across 8 test files -- clear signal a 'restore backup' UI hookup is imminent, at which point the first restore on a multi-child/multi-account device would silently erase a sibling's entire Torah-study history.
finding.recommendation: Thread profileId/accountId into importData() and scope every delete with `..where((tbl) => tbl.profileId.equals(profileId))` (account-level equivalent for accounts/learnerProfiles); extend the round-trip test to seed two profiles and import only one.
acceptance_criteria: New/updated test seeds profile A and profile B, exports+imports only A, and asserts profile B's rows in all 16 tables are byte-for-byte unchanged (not just non-empty).

Every _database.delete(...) call in importData() carries a matching .where(...) scoping clause -- checkable by a Rule-0 grep asserting no bare `delete(_database.` call lacks a following `..where(` in this file.
